comparisons.peer_summary: Net charge-offs increased $1.2 billion to $3.7 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, while loans 30 days or more past due increased $219 million and those 90 days or more past due increased $177 million at December 31, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC report increased delinquency metrics for their credit card portfolios in 2024, driven by similar factors including the maturation/seasoning of recent vintages and macroeconomic pressures. C specifically notes a rise in its 90+ days past due rate due to these vintage maturation and inflation/interest rate pressures, particularly among lower FICO bands. BAC mirrors this trend, reporting an increase in credit card loans 90 days or more past due at year-end 2024, alongside an increase in net charge-offs.

sentences.text: The 90+ days past due delinquency rate increased quarter-over-quarter, primarily driven by seasonality, and increased year-over-year, primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years.
In addition, the increase was driven by macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment, with lower FICO band customers primarily driving the increase.
Net charge-offs increased $1.2 billion to $3.7 billion in 2024 compared to 2023.
Credit card loans 30 days or more past due increased $219 million, and 90 days or more past due increased $177 million at December 31, 2024.
